predecessors.name: House of Ascania
predecessors.text: the Ascanian Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg, 'centered at Wittenberg' (about 4,500-5,000 km2 on the Electorate page)

successors.name: Kingdom of Saxony
successors.text: the electorate 'raised to a kingdom on 20 December 1806'

rulers.name: Frederick Augustus I (Augustus II of Poland)
rulers.title: Elector

rulers.name: Frederick Augustus II (Augustus III of Poland)
rulers.title: Elector

ledger.x: 10 January 1356: the Golden Bull makes the Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg a Prince-Elector.
1423: the Ascanian line gives way to the Wettin.
1423: the Margraviate of Meissen joins the electorate under Frederick I.
7 May 1440: Thuringia reverts to the electorate.
ledger.cp: Landgraviate of Thuringia (Wettin line of Frederick IV)

ledger.x: 1445: the Division of Altenburg gives Thuringia to William III.
ledger.cp: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)

ledger.x: 1446: the Saxon Brother War begins between Frederick II and William III.
ledger.cp: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)

ledger.x: 27 January 1451: the Saxon Brother War ends.
ledger.cp: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)

ledger.x: 1482: Thuringia returns to the electorate.
ledger.cp: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)

ledger.x: 11 November 1485: the Partition of Leipzig divides the Wettin lands, Albert taking the old Margraviate of Meissen (Dresden, Leipzig) as Duke of Saxony and Ernest keeping the electorate.
1547: the capital passes from Wittenberg to Dresden.

1547: after the Battle of Mühlberg the Ernestines lose the tenure of the Vogtland, which Ferdinand I gives to Henry IV of Plauen with Maurice of Saxony as co-tenant (Vogtland page, which gives the year and no month).
ledger.cp: Henry IV of Plauen (Burgraves of Plauen)

ledger.x: 19 May 1547: the Capitulation of Wittenberg gives the electoral title to Maurice of the Albertine line.
19 May 1547: the Ernestines keep their Thuringian and Franconian lands.
19 May 1547: Maurice, Duke of Saxony of the Albertine line, becomes elector and the Albertine duchy joins the electorate.

1559: Henry V and Henry VI of Plauen 'pawned the Vogtland to the Electorate of Saxony in 1559' (a pledge; the infobox gives the annexation as 1563 and the text has Augustus 'acquired the office and towns of Voigtsberg, Oelsnitz, Plauen and Pausa' in 1566).
ledger.cp: Burgraves of Plauen (Henry V and Henry VI)

ledger.x: September 1620: Saxon troops occupy Upper and Lower Lusatia for the emperor.
30 May 1635: the Peace of Prague gives Saxony four Magdeburg towns.
1636: Lusatia is Saxony's by cession.
1636: Ferdinand II cedes Lower and Upper Lusatia to Saxony in perpetuity.
1642: Sweden overruns Saxony.
6 September 1645: the Truce of Kötzschenbroda ends the Swedish occupation of Saxony except for Leipzig and Torgau.
6 September 1645: the Swedes keep Leipzig and Torgau under the Truce of Kötzschenbroda ('Die Städte Leipzig und Torgau bleiben schwedisch besetzt').
30 June 1650: the Swedes leave Leipzig after a tribute is paid.
8 October 1656: Saxe-Weissenfels is cut off as a secundogeniture.
22 April 1657: Saxe-Merseburg is cut off as a secundogeniture.
22 April 1657: Saxe-Zeitz is cut off as a secundogeniture.
1706: the Swedes occupy Saxony.
1707: the Swedes leave Saxony.
1718: Saxe-Zeitz falls back to the electorate.
1738: Saxe-Merseburg falls back to the electorate.
16 May 1746: Saxe-Weissenfels falls back to the electorate.
1756: Prussia attacks and takes Saxony.
15 February 1763: the Treaty of Hubertusburg ends the Prussian hold.
1806: after Jena the French take Dresden.
11 December 1806: the Treaty of Poznań.
20 December 1806: the Electorate of Saxony becomes a kingdom.

wars.name: Saxon Brother War
wars.outcome: The war between Frederick II and his brother William III ended on 27 January 1451 (Naumburg per the Frederick II page, Pforta per the Electorate page) and confirmed the Altenburg partition; William kept Thuringia to his death in 1482.

wars.name: Capitulation of Wittenberg (Battle of Mühlberg)
wars.outcome: Maurice, the Albertine Duke of Saxony, defeated the Ernestine elector John Frederick I at Mühlberg, captured Wittenberg and took the electoral title by the Capitulation of Wittenberg (19 May 1547) together with large parts of the Ernestine lands; the…

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: Saxony occupied Lusatia in 1620 for the emperor and received it in perpetuity in 1636; it joined Sweden in 1631 (Breitenfeld, Lützen), made peace at Prague in 1635 and was overrun by Sweden after Breitenfeld in 1642; the Peace of Westphalia was concluded on…

wars.name: Swedish occupation of Saxony and the Treaty of Altranstädt
wars.outcome: The Swedes occupied Saxony in 1706/07 and the Treaty of Altranstädt forced Augustus II to give up the Polish crown temporarily; he regained it in 1709.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: Frederick of Prussia attacked and captured Saxony in 1756; the Treaty of Hubertusburg (15 February 1763) 'restored the prewar status quo' with no significant border change, and Saxony's great-power status ended.

wars.name: Jena campaign and the Treaty of Poznań
wars.outcome: Saxony fought with Prussia at Jena, was occupied, concluded the Treaty of Poznań with France on 11 December 1806, joined the Confederation of the Rhine and became a kingdom on 20 December 1806.

certainty.note: The Wettin, Ascanian and Thuringian lands were lordships, pledges and divided inheritances; no treaty line of the electorate is dated on the pages opened.
The frontier with Bohemia is sharp from the Treaty of Eger (1459), which 'fixed the borders between Bohemia and Saxony' along the Ore Mountains crest and the middle of the Elbe.
